definitions.explanation: An exaggerated appetite or greed for food — the attitude of wanting as much (or as good) food as possible. Usually used with a light, half-joking tone, often about oneself, but can be critical when used of others. Most commonly appears in the set phrase {食|く}い{意地|いじ}が{張|は}る.

examples.japanese: {食|く}い{意地|いじ}が{張|は}っている。
{彼|かれ}は{食|く}い{意地|いじ}が{張|は}っていて、{人|ひと}の{分|ぶん}まで{食|た}べてしまう。
examples.english: He is so greedy for food that he even eats other people's share.

examples.japanese: ダイエットを{始|はじ}めたのに、{食|く}い{意地|いじ}が{張|は}っていて、どうしても{甘|あま}いものを{我慢|がまん}できない。
examples.english: Even though I've started dieting, I'm so greedy when it comes to food that I just can't hold back from sweets.

notes:
Composed of {食|く}い (eating, nominalized form of {食|く}う "to eat") and {意地|いじ} (willpower, stubbornness, pride). Literally something like "eating stubbornness." The word is most natural in the fixed expression {食|く}い{意地|いじ}が{張|は}る ("one's greed for food is extended/stretched"), which means to be greedy about food.

REGISTER:
Informal and conversational. It is often used self-deprecatingly ("I'm such a glutton") and can be affectionate between friends or family. When used about others without a joking tone, it may sound mildly critical.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食|く}い{意地|いじ}が{張|は}る: to be greedy for food (set phrase)
- {食|く}い{意地|いじ}の{張|は}った{人|ひと}: a person who is greedy for food
- {食|く}い{意地|いじ}が{勝|か}つ: one's greed for food wins out (over willpower)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}: a glutton, a "foodie" — more affectionate; often used of children
- {意地|いじ}{汚|きたな}い: greedy, grasping (not only about food) — harshly critical
- {大食|おおぐ}らい: a big eater — neutral, describes quantity
- {食欲|しょくよく}{旺盛|おうせい}: having a strong appetite — neutral/positive
